newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich urges Clinton to offer fast-track bill.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich urges Clinton to offer fast-track bill.

text.p: House Speaker Newt Gingrich Tuesday urged President Clinton to send Congress legislation restoring fast-trade trade negotiation legislation as soon as possible.
"We'd like to move it as quickly as possible," Gingrich, R-Georgia, told reporters at a meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien. "We really want to pass this bill very rapidly."
But he added: "They (the administration) would have to get votes from Democrats."

The fast-track authority allows the administration to send trade agreements to Congress for approval under a 90-day time limit with no amendments allowed. The authority lapsed in 1994 and Gingrich said the administration was behind schedule in proposing legislation to renew it. Gingrich said it was needed to expand the North American Free Trade Agreement to nations in South America, a move Chretien endorsed.

Gingrich said there were no major problems between the United States and Canada even though Canada opposes the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which seeks to punish some companies in third countries that do business with Cuba.
